admissions_mode.quote: Students in this program are required to do two lab rotations as part of their training; a third rotation is optional but encouraged.

contact_faculty_advice.value: Not necessary to contact faculty before applying; rotation advisors are selected after admission. GCB asks that application questions go to the BGS Admissions Office, not admissions committee members.

stipend.note: GCB admissions page: accepted students receive tuition, health insurance and a twelve-month stipend.

guaranteed_years.value: Full fellowship (stipend, tuition, fees, health insurance) guaranteed for the duration of training while in good academic standing (BGS anticipates 5-6 years)
guaranteed_years.quote: Students in BGS are provided with a full-fellowship guarantee to cover stipend, tuition, fees, and health insurance for the duration of their training as a student in good academic standing.
guaranteed_years.note: BGS Admissions FAQs: 'awarded financial support for the anticipated five to six years required to attain the doctoral degree.'

pr_domestic.quote: 962 from US citizens or permanent residents of the US, and 694 from international citizens
pr_domestic.note: Indirect: no GCB or BGS page explicitly defines 'domestic applicant'. This quote is from CAMB, a sibling BGS graduate group sharing the central BGS application/admissions committee, which counts permanent residents with US citizens and separately from 'international citizens'. BGS also groups PRs with citizens for training-grant eligibility (student-funding.html). BGS FAQ limits only 'international students' ('we can only accept a small number of international students'). t32_citizen_pr_only.quote: Eligible students (generally US citizens or permanent residents) may be appointed to a training grant at some point in their PhD training.

waiver_conditions.value: English test (TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo) required only for applicants whose native language is not English; waived for applicants who have or will have obtained a degree from a US or other approved English-instructed institution (no waiver request needed; confirmed during review).
waiver_conditions.quote: Applicants whose native language is not English are required to take an English proficiency exam (either the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo test); this requirement is waived for applicants who have or will have obtained a degree from a US or other approved English-instructed institution.
waiver_conditions.note: Same wording on phd-application-information.html. FAQ also: 'You do not need a waiver for this - we'll confirm this as part of our review process.'

waiver_basis.quote: this requirement is waived for applicants who have or will have obtained a degree from a US or other approved English-instructed institution
waiver_basis.note: Requirement applies only to non-native English speakers; exemption otherwise by degree.

us_degree_waives.quote: We will waive the TOEFL requirement for students who have/will have obtained a degree from a U.S. or other approved English-instructed institution. You do not need a waiver for this
us_degree_waives.note: 'have/will have obtained' covers a US bachelor's still in progress at application time, e.g. Emory degree conferred spring 2027 (before Fall 2027 matriculation).

pr_exempt.note: Official BGS text (Admissions FAQs, PhD Application Information) does not mention citizenship or permanent-resident status for the English test: it applies to applicants whose native language is not English and is waived for anyone with a US (or approved English-instructed) degree. So PR status itself is not a stated basis; a PR with a US bachelor's is exempt via the degree waiver (see us_degree_waives).

min_total.quote: There are no minimum score requirements.

min_subscores.quote: There are no minimum score requirements.

validity_rule.value: Scores more than 2 years old are not issued by ETS and must be retaken; official reports must reach BGS by the application deadline
validity_rule.quote: ETS will not issue TOEFL scores that are more than 2 years old. Applicants who have expired scores must retake the test(s).
validity_rule.note: No explicit reference date (application vs. enrollment) given beyond ETS's 2-year reporting limit.

di_code.quote: Please enter the code 2900 on your TOEFL test.

self_report_accepted.quote: In order for your application to be considered complete, official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo score reports must be received by the BGS office by the application deadline.

gre_policy.quote: Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General test scores are not considered. The Subject Test in Physics or Mathematics is optional.

waiver_conditions.value: ELP must be demonstrated only by applicants whose native language is not English. Ways: (1) bachelor's/master's/doctoral degree from an accredited English-medium institution (for an English-speaking country such as the US: in residence in that country for the full duration of enrollment; no MOI documentation needed for US degrees); (2) official TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo score (BPSD requires the Graduate School 'Recommended' level); (3) previous UW graduate degree or current UW graduate enrollment. Grad School FAQ: a U.S. degree conferred by the program start completes the requirement (formally 'no waivers', but the degree satisfies it).
waiver_conditions.quote: An earned and bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree (or an internationally recognized academic degree at the same level) from an accredited institution for which English was the medium of instruction.
waiver_conditions.note: Residency condition (same page): 'For institutions located in an English-speaking country: The student must have been in residence in that country for the full duration of enrollment in the degree program'. The United States is on the list of countries exempt from MOI documentation. For the applicant (US PR, Emory bachelor's conferred spring 2027, before Autumn 2027 start): the Emory degree satisfies the ELP requirement if they were resident in the US throughout enrollment; no test needed. For the required 2nd-year TA appointment, Policy 5.2 likewise accepts a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited US institution with English medium of instruction (https://grad.uw.edu/policies/5-2-conditions-of-appointment-for-tas-who-are-not-native-speakers-of-english/).

waiver_basis.quote: English language proficiency (ELP) is required for graduate study at the University of Washington. Therefore, every applicant whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency.
waiver_basis.note: Exempt if native English speaker (as self-declared on the application); otherwise satisfied by an English-medium degree (3.2.1 item 1), a test score, or a previous/current UW graduate degree/enrollment. No citizenship/residency-status basis.

us_degree_waives.quote: If your U.S. degree will be conferred by the start of the program you are applying to, the conferral of your U.S. degree will complete the Graduate School’s English proficiency requirement.
us_degree_waives.note: Answer to FAQ 'I will receive a degree from the US, can I be waived from the English language proficiency test score requirement?'. Technically 'This school does not grant waivers', but the US degree satisfies the requirement; applicants receiving a U.S. degree may leave the test section blank ('You may leave this section blank on your application, as you will be receiving a U.S. degree.'). An official transcript with degree posted is required before the first quarter. Applies to an Emory bachelor's conferred spring 2027 for Autumn 2027 entry (subject to the Policy 3.2 US-residency-during-enrollment condition).

pr_exempt.quote: Graduate School admission requirements and application procedures are the same for all applicants regardless of citizenship and visa status.
pr_exempt.note: Permanent-resident status by itself does not exempt: the requirement depends on native language ('Demonstration of English proficiency is required of all non-native English speakers.' on the same page). A PR who is a native English speaker is not required to demonstrate ELP; a non-native PR with a US degree satisfies it via the degree (see us_degree_waives). BPSD's criteria page phrases it as 'International students must meet all English language proficiency requirements set by the Graduate School', but the Graduate School rule (Policy 3.2 / BPSD Application Process page) is 'every applicant whose native language is not English'.
